question: A profit earned when an item is sold for ₹4,000 is ten times the loss incurred when it is sold for ₹ 2,790. At what price should the item be sold if it is desired to make a profit of 20%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between the two selling prices = ₹4,000 − ₹2,790 = ₹1,210.

Ratio of Profit to Loss = 10 : 1. Total parts = 10 + 1 = 11 parts.

11 parts = 1,210 ⇒ 1 part (Loss) = 1,210 ÷ 11 = ₹110.

Cost Price (CP) = ₹2,790 + ₹110 = ₹2,900.

Selling Price for 20% profit = ₹2,900 × 1.20 = ₹3,480.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = ₹2,790 (Loss incurred)

Selling Price 2 (SP₂) = ₹4,000 (Profit earned)

Profit = 10
